about: The balance simulator (`python -m bitminer.sim`): a bot plays whole games of Secure the Base through the same controls you have, with no graphics, and reports whether the pacing guide's targets are met. `step_rate` is how many steps a second it plays at (the game plays the same at any rate) and `minutes` how long each game lasts. `plan` is what the bot buys, in this order, phase by phase (the Planned spending column of the pacing guide's budget); a key the shop doesn't sell yet is skipped and listed in the report, and `sentry_missile:3` means that sentry at tier 3. `presets` are three kinds of player. `aim_error` is how far off its aim wanders, in degrees. `pause` is the average seconds it wastes after finishing each job, and `shop_seconds` how long each station visit takes. `cruise` is the fastest it flies, `tow_speed` the fastest it tows. It fights enemies within `engage` of it, holding between `keep` (nearest, furthest) from them, and swaps the auto cannon for the sniper beyond `sniper_from`. It buys a hull repair when it visits the station below `repair_at` of its hull. `bot` holds the bot's own habits: it looks for ore within `mine_range` of home base and rocks to tow within `tow_range` of the ring, loads a drill once it holds `load_at` ore, flies home once it carries `home_at` ore, puts the ring `ring_range` (nearest, furthest) from home base, gives up on a job after `give_up` seconds and leaves that rock alone for `avoid` seconds, and counts a structure as under attack for `alarm` seconds after it is hit. `marks` are the pass marks from the pacing guide: each is the median over the seeds, and passes when it is between `low` and `high` (minutes, or a count for deaths). `window` is how many minutes the report averages income over when it looks for the minute combat income passes mining income.
